tldr: This is a loose topical cluster, not one event: three unrelated items that each use "routing" to cut inference cost or latency at a different layer. OpenRouter rebuilt provider routing in its hosted gateway on Oct 30, and a Show HN on Nov 7 introduced Sibyl, an immutable local inference appliance with routing built in.
whats_new: The arXiv paper C²-Routing (Nov 10) moves routing to the input layer, pairing image cropping with compression as a model-agnostic way to shrink what a vision-language model must process for visual question answering.
why_it_matters: "Routing" now names three separate cost and latency levers (which provider serves a request, which local backend runs it, and how much input reaches the model), and each one is tuned and evaluated differently.

beats.headline: OpenRouter rebuilds provider routing for better, faster inference
beats.summary: Routing at the hosted-gateway layer: choosing which provider serves a request.

beats.headline: Sibyl packages a local inference stack as an immutable appliance with routing
beats.summary: A solo side project, described by its author as early days, that puts routing in a portable self-hosted box configured through a UI.

beats.headline: C²-Routing applies routing to VLM inputs: cropping plus compression
beats.summary: A paper on model-agnostic input reduction for visual question answering, unrelated to either product above.

open_questions: Does OpenRouter publish latency or success-rate numbers that quantify the rebuilt provider routing?
Does Sibyl's routing select among local models and backends only, or can it also fall back to hosted providers?
How much accuracy does C²-Routing give up for its input reduction, and does the result hold across VLMs beyond those the paper tests?
take_for_builders: Treat these as three independent decisions. If you send traffic through OpenRouter, re-measure latency and provider distribution after the routing rebuild; evaluate the appliance and the paper on their own evidence before adopting either.
